first.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ, which is the more immediate operational risk than the 4% onboarding decline. memory_91 shows activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to first meaningful action—this is directly addressable. memory_31 and memory_86 both support that simplification and shortening onboarding drove adoption, but activation_messaging targets the existing funnel without the retention risk that memory_73 flagged for promotional_pricing. Referral incentives (memory_57) work on established customers, not the activation problem. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) addresses pipeline quality but not the SMB activation leak or competitive pricing pressure. Activation messaging is low-risk, targets the immediate metric decline, and has proven precedent. Verifying memory_31 and memory_91 will confirm the magnitude of prior lift and any boundary conditions before scaling.

mid.rationale: Activation messaging demonstrated +6% activation lift with +1% retention gain in exp_91, making it the safest high-impact lever available. The verified source confirms week-one engagement +11%, which directly addresses the 6% QoQ activation decline. Unlike promotional_pricing (memory_73, which materially damaged 30-day retention), activation_messaging improved retention. Signup simplification (exp_31) showed +9% activation but -1% retention risk on SMB and was segment-specific. In-product activation messaging is segment-agnostic, proven, and retention-positive. The competitor pricing threat affects price-sensitive SMB, but referral_incentive works only on established customers (memory_57), and enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) does not address the activation metric decline or SMB acquisition pressure. Activation_messaging scales cleanly to a standard experiment and avoids the trade-offs that plague promotional pricing. This preserves long-term qualified revenue by improving engagement without sacrificing retention.

final2.rationale: The competitor price cut creates urgency, but memory_73 explicitly warns that promotional_pricing materially reduced 30-day retention and should not be generalized as a growth strategy. Matching pricing in a race-to-the-bottom destroys long-term qualified revenue—the primary objective. The doubled churn conversations are a symptom of disengagement, not primarily price elasticity at this stage. Activation_messaging (+6% activation, +1% retention) remains the highest-confidence, lowest-risk lever that improves product stickiness and perceived value realization. Better engagement and early meaningful action increase customer lifetime value and reduce price-sensitivity. Referral_incentive works only on established customers (not at-risk SMB). Simplify_onboarding carries -1% retention risk on SMB per exp_31. Enterprise_sales_assist does not address SMB retention. Competing on activation and value delivery preserves the customer relationship more durably than competing on price. The activation_messaging experiment runs in parallel to churn mitigation conversations while protecting long-term margin and revenue quality.
